title: Prospective Evaluation of Response to Treatment in Younger Adult Patients (18-60 Years) With Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
official: Prospective Evaluation of Response to Treatment by Analysis of Measurable Residual Disease in Younger Adult Patients (18-60 Years) With Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). The Backbone InterGroup (BIG)-2 Umbrella Trial From the Acute Leukemia French Intergroup (ALFA, FILO)
summary:
The treatment of younger AML patients fit for intensive chemotherapy (IC) has long been based on a combination of an anthracycline and cytarabine as induction, followed by high-dose cytarabine (HDAC) consolidation, and possibly allogeneic stem-cell transplantation at least in non-favorable risk AML patients. Even if new agents like gemtuzumab ozogamicin (GO), FLT3 inhibitors, or CPX-351 have been approved to treat some patient subsets, there has been no major therapeutic advances to date in this field.

The first multicenter trial from the ALFA-FILO intergroup (Backbone InterGroup trial-1, BIG-1; NCT02416388; PHRC2010-03) randomly explored various standard intensive chemotherapy strategies, including higher-dose idarubicin vs. high-dose daunorubicin (DNR) and intermediate-dose cytarabine (IDAC) vs. HDAC in patients (18-60 years) with newly-diagnosed AML. This first part of the study, which enrolled 1405 participants between 01/2015 and 05/2019, showed that the benefit/risk ratio favored high-dose DNR for remission induction and IDAC consolidation, establishing the national standard treatment for younger AML patients. Six-year OS was 53.4% showing that there is still considerable room for improvement in this younger patient population.

High-throughput sequencing and multiparametric flow cytometry have significantly improved prognostic classifications and the evaluation of response to therapy through the quantification of measurable residual disease (MRD). Many studies have shown that the higher the MRD, the higher the risk of relapse and death; and recent guidelines have included MRD in the response criteria. Achieving complete remission without MRD is a major goal after first-line treatment to guide subsequent treatments, including transplantation. Furthermore, MRD follow-up in patients who achieved complete remission is becoming a major issue, as patients treated for molecular relapse appear to have a better prognosis than patients treated for morphological relapse. Preliminary data also showed encouraging results from salvage treatment at the time of MRD relapse.

Quizartinib (a second-generation FLT3-ITD inhibitor) and venetoclax (the first-in-class BCL-2 inhibitor) have been recently approved for the treatment of AML. Quizartinib was approved on the basis of a placebo-controlled trial but its added value compared to midostaurin (first FLT3 inhibitor available in this indication since 2018) has never been prospectively explored. Although venetoclax was approved for first line therapy of patients who are unfit for intensive chemotherapy, it is widely used in relapsed or refractory younger patients. Venetoclax combined with intensive salvage chemotherapy is feasible and induce a high rate of CR. However, no prospective, randomized trial demonstrated venetoclax efficacy in this setting.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age ≥ 18 years and \< 61 years
2. With a newly diagnosed de novo acute myeloid leukemia, or secondary acute myeloid leukemia arising from a previously known myelodysplastic syndrome, or post cytotoxic therapy-related acute myeloid leukemia, according to the 2022 World Health Organisation classification
3. No prior treatment for acute myeloid leukemia (with the exception of hydroxyurea) or for myelodysplastic syndrome (with the exception of hematopoietic growth factors)
4. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status ≤ 3
5. Eligible to induction chemotherapy
6. No contraindication to anthracyclines: decompensated or uncontrolled heart failure, recent myocardial infarction, current signs of cardiac impairment, uncontrolled arrhythmias, or left ventricular ejection fraction \< 50%
7. Total bilirubin ≤ 2 x upper limit of normal, Aspartate Aminotransferase and Alanine Aminotransferase ≤ 2.5 X upper limit of normal, creatinine \< 150 µmol/l, unless acute myeloid leukemia-related values
8. Women of childbearing potential should use appropriate methods of contraception
9. Health insurance coverage
10. Signed written informed consent

Additional inclusion criteria for sub-study 1 11 1. Presence of FLT3 internal tandem duplication activating mutation in bone marrow (allelic ratio ≥ 0.03) 12-1. Receiving standard 7+3 induction chemotherapy regimen as specified in the protocol 13 1. Serum electrolytes within the institution's normal limits: potassium, calcium (total calcium, calcium corrected for serum albumin in case of hypoalbuminemia, or ionized calcium), and magnesium.

Additional inclusion criteria for sub-study 2 11-2. Refractory (no response) or CR/CRh/CRi with positive Measurable Residual Disease by Multiparameter Flow Cytometry in bone marrow (≥ 0.1%) after one cycle of 7+3 induction 12 2. Eligible for a second cycle of intensive chemotherapy

Additional inclusion criteria for sub-study 3 11 3. CR/CRh/CRi without Measurable Residual Disease by Multiparameter Flow Cytometry in bone marrow (\< 0.1% OR \< Limit of Detection) after one cycle of 7+3 induction.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Patients with secondary acute myeloid leukemia arising from a previously known myeloproliferative neoplasm according to the 2022 World Health Organisation classification
2. Patients with acute promyelocytic leukemia, as confirmed either by t(15;17) or by the presence of promyelocytic leukemia::RARA fusion transcripts
3. Patients with t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2)/BCR::ABL1 or previous Ph1+ disorder (chronic myelogenous leukemia)
4. Severe psychiatric or organic disorder, supposed to be independent from acute myeloid leukemia , that would contraindicate treatment, including allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
5. Any psychological, familial, social, or geographic reason that would compromise clinical follow up
6. Prior cancer, if not stable for at least two years, except in-situ carcinoma and skin carcinoma
7. With uncontrolled severe infection at study entry
8. Patients with uncontroled Human Immunodeficiency Virus-1 and -2 infection, or active hepatitis virus B or C infection
9. Pregnant or lactating women
10. Legal incapacity (patients under tutorship, curatorship or judicial protection)

Additional exclusion criteria for sub-study 1 11 1. Patients with Core-Binding Factor Acute myeloid leukemia 12 1. Prior treatment with quizartinib or other FLT3 inhibitors 13 1. Uncontrolled or significant cardiovascular disease, including any of the following:

* Bradycardia \< 50 beats per minute
* QTcF interval \>450 msec
* Diagnosis of or suspicion of long QT syndrome (including family history of long QT syndrome)
* Systolic blood pressure ≥180 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure ≥110 mm Hg
* History of clinically relevant ventricular arrhythmias (e.g., ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, or torsade de pointes)
* History of second (Mobitz II) or third-degree heart block (patients with pacemakers were eligible if they had no history of fainting or clinically relevant arrhythmias while using the pacemaker)
* History of uncontrolled angina pectoris or myocardial infarction within 6 months before screening
* History of New York Heart Association class 3 or 4 heart failure
* Left ventricular ejection fraction ≤45% or less than the institutional lower limit of normal per multigated acquisition scan or echocardiogram done within 30 days before randomization
* Complete left bundle branch block 14-1. Uncorrected Grade 3 or 4 hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia or hypocalcemia. Subjects with Grade 1 or 2 electrolyte abnormalities can be enrolled while electrolytes are being corrected.

15-1. Treatment with any strong or moderate CYP3A inducers within 2 weeks or 5 half-lives of randomization whichever is longer

Additional exclusion criteria for sub-study 2 11 2. Patients with acute myeloid leukemia with FLT3 internal tandem duplication mutation without Core-Binding Factor 12 2. Uncontrolled infection such as sepsis, or multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, uncontrolled fever 13 2. Documented uncontrolled fungal infection (positive blood test and cultures) 14 2. Prior venetoclax exposure

Additional exclusion criteria for sub-study 3 11 3. Patients with acute myeloid leukemia with FLT3 internal tandem duplication mutation without Core-Binding Factor
